note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Prototype misalignment under model heterogeneity motivates bilateral (feature + logit) alignment, validated empirically

nodes.name: Homogeneity assumption unrealistic
nodes.description: Most multimodal federated learning methods assume all clients deploy an identical architecture, but real clients are heterogeneous in hardware resources and multimodal data distributions.

nodes.name: Heterogeneous encoders give incompatible feature spaces
nodes.description: Heterogeneous encoders map multimodal data into disparate embedding spaces, so prototypes of the same class from different clients reside in incompatible feature spaces.

nodes.name: Direct prototype aggregation contaminates knowledge
nodes.description: Direct server aggregation of misaligned prototypes pulls the global prototype toward class decision boundaries and can make performance fall below purely local training.

nodes.name: Logit prototypes are naturally aligned
nodes.description: Logits reside in a shared semantic space across heterogeneous models because each dimension corresponds to a specific class, so logit prototypes need no extra alignment.

nodes.name: Entropy-weighted logit aggregation
nodes.description: MFedPBA aggregates logit prototypes with weights proportional to inverse entropy (plus epsilon), giving lower-uncertainty clients higher weight to form a more reliable global logit prototype.

nodes.name: Server autoencoder aligns feature prototypes
nodes.description: The server uses modality-specific encoders and a shared decoder to project feature prototypes of different modalities and dimensionalities into a unified space, trained with reconstruction, inter-modal contrastive and Gromov-Wasserstein alignment losses.

nodes.name: GW distance fits heterogeneous spaces
nodes.description: The Gromov-Wasserstein distance compares intra-space pairwise distance structures, so it needs no direct correspondence between feature dimensions and suits heterogeneous settings.

nodes.name: GW alignment of feature and logit spaces
nodes.description: The intra-modal alignment loss computes entropy-regularized GW distance (Sinkhorn) between each modality's class-relation cost matrix and that of the global logit prototype, preserving topological consistency.

nodes.name: Client local update
nodes.description: Clients distill the global feature prototypes (MSE alignment) and global logit prototypes (KL divergence) into local training together with cross-entropy, with total loss L_ce + lambda1 L_fea + lambda2 L_logit.

nodes.name: Non-convex convergence
nodes.description: Under stated assumptions, each client's local model converges at a non-convex rate O(1/T).

nodes.name: Consistent accuracy gains
nodes.description: MFedPBA achieves the best test accuracy on Caltech101, Reuters, NUS-WIDE and Youtube under M2, M1+ and M1 partitions, e.g. 49.04 vs 45.29 for the best baseline on Caltech101 M2 and 47.92 vs 45.53 on Youtube M2.

nodes.name: Scales to more clients
nodes.description: MFedPBA maintains superior performance with larger client numbers (e.g. Reuters K100: 57.83 vs 56.64 for the best baseline).

nodes.name: FedProto sometimes below local training
nodes.description: In several settings FedProto underperforms Local training, confirming that naive aggregation of misaligned prototypes causes knowledge contamination.

nodes.name: Ablation: server modules needed
nodes.description: Removing any server-side module significantly lowers accuracy on Caltech101 M2, and removing the reconstruction loss causes the most severe drop through representation collapse in the latent space.

nodes.name: Low communication overhead
nodes.description: MFedPBA's bidirectional cost is K^2 C (M_k d_D + d_C), only a negligible increase over FedProto since the number of classes is far smaller than model parameter counts.

isolated_nodes.name: Modality imbalance gap
isolated_nodes.description: Existing MFL methods assume balanced modality distributions or restrict to bimodal/identical-modality settings, failing to capture imbalance in modality availability across clients.

isolated_nodes.name: FedMBridge overhead
isolated_nodes.description: FedMBridge's topology-aware hypernetwork incurs prohibitive communication overhead that scales poorly with model complexity and modality count.

isolated_nodes.name: Prototype instability of FedTGP
isolated_nodes.description: Prototype-based baselines, particularly FedTGP, fluctuate during training because of erratic server prototype updates in multimodal scenarios.

isolated_nodes.name: Feature dimension trade-off
isolated_nodes.description: Small feature dimensions cause underfitting while excessively large ones add redundant noise; on Youtube most methods perform best at d_D=48.

isolated_nodes.name: Hyperparameter robustness
isolated_nodes.description: MFedPBA stays above accuracy 46 and outperforms all baselines across most lambda1/lambda2 values on Youtube, while excessively large loss weights degrade performance.

isolated_nodes.name: Server-side computation
isolated_nodes.description: The framework offloads the main computational burden to the resource-rich server, with only O(C^2) extra client overhead for the KL divergence.

structural_reasoning: Argument runs from the heterogeneity/misalignment problem, to logit-prototype and GW feature alignment design, to client update, convergence and experiments.
